audits.title: When Psychosis is Not Psychosis: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Delirium Misdiagnosis Across Hospital Departments
audits.standard: CAM-ICU delirium screening before psychiatry referral
audits.setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital; referrals from Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Orthopaedics and ICU

cycle1.result: 82/130 (63%) referrals for suspected psychosis were delirium; CAM-ICU use 0%; mean time to delirium management 22 hours.

audits.intervention: Four-week CAM-ICU training: didactic sessions (Medicine, Surgery), bedside demonstrations (ICU, Orthopaedics), and quick-reference materials with brief ward teaching (Obstetrics and Gynaecology).

cycle2.result: Misdiagnosis fell to 39/126 (31%); CAM-ICU uptake 56%; mean time to delirium management 11 hours.

audits.other_findings: Bedside training gave the highest uptake (ICU 72%, Orthopaedics 65%); orthopaedic misdiagnosis fell from 62% to 25%.
audits.citation: Khakha R, Rani S. When Psychosis is Not Psychosis: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Delirium Misdiagnosis Across Hospital Departments. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S165-S166. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11410.

audits.title: 45 Quality Improvement Project on Delirium Care in Older Patients at Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (MYHT)
audits.standard: NICE CG103 and SIGN 157: delirium diagnosis with CAM or 4AT and management with care plan
audits.setting: Frailty admission unit, Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (large district general)

cycle1.result: CAM or 4AT used in 32.5%; delirium care plan in 20%.

audits.intervention: Delirium care checklist sticker, brief education sessions for ward doctors and reminder emails over 6 weeks

cycle2.result: Sticker use fell from 57% in week 1 to 0% in week 6; 4AT 57%, 50%, 100% in first 3 weeks then 40%, 4.2%, 1.3%; care plan 42% and 37% in first 2 weeks, 0% by week 6.

audits.standard: 4AT delirium screening of patients aged over 65 on arrival and at 48 hours
audits.setting: Surgical Assessment Unit, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton

cycle1.result: 36% likely to have delirium on 4AT; 5% coded as delirium and 19% had delirium documented in notes; average 4AT completion 40%.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles introducing 4AT and delirium sections in care plans, plus teaching and supporting materials around the PINCHME acronym for SAU staff.

cycle2.result: Average 4AT completion rose from 40% to 64%, reaching 100% after interventions but falling back between them.

audits.title: Closing the gap in postoperative delirium detection: addressing low screening rates in the surgical recovery room.
audits.standard: NICE delirium guidance: high-risk patients (age over 65, cognitive impairment, hip fracture) screened with a validated tool (4AT or CAM) before PACU discharge. Target at least 50% adherence within 1 month of launch.
audits.setting: Post-Anaesthesia Care Unit (main and burns theatres), Chelsea and Westminster Hospital (large tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: 3/130 (2.3%) at-risk patients screened for delirium in PACU; nurse confidence median 7/10 and guideline clarity median 4/10.

audits.intervention: PDSA 1: new trust-wide perioperative delirium guideline. PDSA 2: 4AT made easily accessible on electronic systems, PACU discharge checklist updated to require screening, simplified guidance signposted, daily list review at morning huddles to flag at-risk patients, staff education, and leadership engagement using coding/funding data.

cycle2.result: 48/67 (71.64%) at-risk patients screened (p<0.0001); 81.50% in final week; nurse confidence and guideline clarity both median 10/10 (p<0.0001).

audits.other_findings: PDSA cycle 1 (29 March to 12 April 2025) screening 15/49 (30.61%). Of 63 screened, 11 (17.46%) scored 4+ suggesting delirium; medical team pathway for positive screens not yet formalised.
audits.citation: Dave S, Vizcaychipi M, Paul J, Diez Martin I. Closing the gap in postoperative delirium detection: addressing low screening rates in the surgical recovery room. BMJ Open Qual. 2026;15(3):e003647. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003647. PMID: 42392679.
